SHUNT FIELD CHARACTERISTICS
The DC Shunt Field motor is generally used for industrial applications.
DISCUSSION
In this lesson, you will explore the characteristics of this type of motor.
As you know, all motors share certain characteristics......
Each of these characteristics can be measured or calculated.
Let's begin by calculating torque in a shunt field motor...
There is a relatively simple formula for calculating the torque of a Shunt motor.
The equation states that the output torque of a motor is the product of the armature current (I ), field coil current (I ) and the physical characteristics of the field (K).
Throughout this lesson and future lessons assume that K has a value of 1. This will simplify calculations.

Let's examine the effects of the second characteristic of DC shunt field motors, CEMF.
As motor shaft speed increases, CEMF increases. They are directly proportional.
DEFINITION
CEMF opposes the original applied voltage that induces motor action.
CEMF acts as another voltage source opposing E ..........
Because of CEMF, I does not equal the applied voltage divided by the resistance of the armature.
I equals the applied voltage minus CEMF divided by the resistance of the armature.

The last important element of DC shunt motors is speed control.
Varying the applied voltage lowers the current through both the armature and the field, this increases RPM.
Resistors can also be used to lower the current through the field coil.
This will decrease the strength of the field coil, decreasing RPM.
This method is called shunt field control.

The last basic characteristic of DC shunt field motors is Speed.
Recall that as speed increases, CEMF increases and torque decreases.
The effect speed has on torque can be easily seen using the DC Shunt Motor schematic.
As speed increases, CEMF increases. As a result, I decreases....
Torque equals I x I x K. If speed increases then torque decreases due to I decreasing.
In other words, as speed increases, I decreases.
As speed decreases, Torque increases (due to I increasing as CEMF decreases) and I increases.
In a DC shunt motor, I is not affected by changes in speed.
This is why DC Shunt Motors have a higher torque value at faster RPM than Series DC Motors.
Another factor affecting speed is the LOAD.................
As a load increases, RPM decreases.........................
As RPM decreases, CEMF decreases, increasing torque.
The only new concept is the effect of a load on RPM. All other relationships remain the same.
You will see the effects of a load on RPM in the experiment.
